newsitem.title: UK: Emerging debt quiet as traders wait for U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Emerging debt quiet as traders wait for U.S. data.

text.p: Trading in emerging market debt was subdued on Friday morning with dealers once again waiting for key U.S. economic data to surface.
"The market is very quiet, as it has been all week," a debt trader at a German bank in Frankfurt said.
U.S. retail sales and producer price data reports were due to be published at 1230 GMT.
Financial markets generally remain edgy about the prospects for U.S. inflation and interest rates, and the data will be closely watched.

Hungary reported an 18.8 percent annual inflation rate for March, a level the National Bank of Hungary's deputy president Gyorgy Szapary said was "a very good result because that's when energy price increases were first reflected."
Hungarian energy prices were increased by 25-30 percent in January, said Szapary, in London for a conference on central and eastern European capital markets.
Szapary said: "(Inflation) could be down to 17 percent or better by December." Hungary has an inflation rate target of 16-18 percent for the end of the year.
